statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail moves from 15 to 16 because the cross-asset backdrop firmed while the index range held. NQ futures were verified at 29,160.50, down 288.25 points or 0.98%, inside a 29,044.25 to 29,508.25 session range. Cash NAS100 at 29,134.68 has eased from 29,180.33 an hour ago but the 29,038.22 opening-auction low is untested for a fourth cash hour, leaving a roughly 212-point band that has contained the whole session. VIX re-firmed to 17.73 from 17.23 while holding below its 18.05 high, the ten-year sits at 4.946% at the top of its session range, and Brent at $108.03 is near its $108.32 high. Mean reversion has continued to function, so tail stays in the low band.
recommendation: Tail at 16 maps the policy state to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution false under the fixed repository mapping. The danger window remains drawn narrowly around 12:30 to 14:00 UTC on 11 September, covering the August consumer price release, the first hour of post-release price discovery and the 13:30 UTC cash open. Oracle's results after today's close and the 21:00 UTC call are treated as scheduled checkpoints inside the forecast rather than grounds for widening the window, because Oracle is NYSE-listed and reaches the Nasdaq-100 only indirectly. Stress at 86 is the elevated part of this assessment and does not by itself change the mapped state.
headline: NQ at 29,160.50 and cash NAS100 at 29,134.68 ease back inside a session range whose 29,038.22 low has now held four cash hours; tail edges from 15 to 16 as the ten-year prints 4.946% at its session high, Brent holds $108.03 and VIX re-firms to 17.73.
body:
The hour brought a modest deterioration in the backdrop without a change in structure. Cash NAS100 eased from 29,180.33 to 29,134.68, down 0.98% on the day, and NQ futures sit at 29,160.50, also down 0.98%. The 29,038.22 opening-auction low is still untested, now for a fourth cash hour, and the roughly 212-point band between it and the 29,250.41 high has contained the entire session. Price has traded in both directions inside that band all afternoon, which is the observation that matters most for the framework used here: tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach, not the size of the move.

What firmed is the cross-asset picture around that range. The ten-year yield is at 4.946%, the top of its 4.879 to 4.946 session range and the highest since 2023; the two-year is at 4.57%, up about twelve basis points; the thirty-year at 5.35% is the highest since 2007. Brent at $108.03 is up 6.74% and close to its $108.32 high, with the move traced to intensified attacks on shipping in the Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab routes. VIX has re-firmed to 17.73 from 17.23 an hour ago while staying under the 18.05 session high. Delayed latest-session context from the shared collector shows the semiconductor complex broadly lower, with six of seven names negative and a mean change near minus 2.5%, alongside a split megacap tape. That context is supporting evidence, not live price-path evidence, and is treated accordingly.

The macro input for the session was the August producer price report at 12:30 UTC: final demand up 0.4% on the month and 5.4% over twelve months, above the 5.3% consensus, with over three-quarters of the goods increase traced to energy and diesel prices up 24.1%. Rate expectations moved with it, and traders were pricing roughly a 70% chance of a hike at the 15-16 September meeting against 62% before the release. That combination raises stress to 86, and stress alone does not change the mapped policy state.

Tail moves from 15 to 16 rather than further, because the amplifiers that firmed are cross-asset rather than structural. There has been no new session low, retracements have continued to occur, and the index has rotated inside its band rather than extending after failed pullbacks. The next observable checkpoints are whether the 29,038.22 low survives the final cash hour and how the market absorbs Oracle's fiscal Q1 2027 results after the close. The window's dominant scheduled risk remains the August consumer price index at 12:30 UTC tomorrow, which is where the published danger window sits.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 18:00 UTC on 9 September to 17:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 12 with a mixed read, troughs at 8 to 9 across the U.S. close and the first overnight hours, and holds a 9 to 11 band through the Asian and European morning. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and a 24 peak at 13:00 UTC covering post-release discovery and the cash open. The last four slots record the decay back into range, 17 then 14, a 16 tick as yields and oil extended, and 15 at 17:00 UTC. Stress never left the extreme band, running 80 to 86 throughout, which is the persistent feature of this window: a difficult, high-volatility tape in which mean reversion nonetheless kept working.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with the session low still holding and closes in the U.S. mid-morning after the August consumer price release. Conditional tail starts at 16 in the current 18:00 UTC hour, steps to 18 for the last full hour before the cash close, and reaches an afternoon peak of 19 across the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots covering the close and Oracle's scheduled results and call into thin futures liquidity. It then decays through 17 and 14 into the late evening and settles to an 11 floor across the Asian hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. From the European open the path rebuilds gradually, 12 through 14, reaching 16 in the final hour before the release. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot that contains the CPI print and 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot where post-release discovery overlaps the cash open, both mapping to WATCH and neither reaching the block threshold, since no post-release price path is observed yet. The path then eases to 19 at the University of Michigan release, 17, and 15 for the last two slots. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout, peaking at 89 across the two CPI hours, and confidence declines from 88 to 70 with distance from observed evidence.
